doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Blakey's itinerary: European tours and the U.S. club circuit
summary: He lists Europe, Birdland, the Jazz Workshop in San Francisco, Chicago's Jazz Showcase, Minneapolis, Detroit's Minor Key and Cleveland.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Give us some sense of what your itinerary was. Tell me about what …

Well, Los Angeles, uh, Europe, uh, tours of Europe, you know, which is a, a succession of cities uh, you know, Switzerland or Germany or Italy or … and the like. And uh, uh the Netherlands uh, everywhere. I don't think we went to Spain, but we certainly went to France and uh, uh … It was just a magnificent uh itinerary.
Was there a club circuit for you in the States?

Uh, well uh, yeah. We played uh Birdland in New York, uh, was our main uh place in New York to play. Uh, San Francisco, the Jazz Workshop, in those days. Uh Chicago uh was uh, the uh, Joe Siegel's place on the southside – Jazz Showcase, I guess you can call it. He still uses that uh name. And uh, yeah, Minneapolis …

Oh yeah, Detroit, yeah. I remember a place named the Minor Key and uh yeah, we had a, we had a club circuit in the, in the States. Uh, once in a while we would go to a, a, a, uh, an institution of learning [chuckles], you know. Uh, university or so and uh …

Yes. We hit Cleveland, I remember hitting Cleveland. And uh, oh man, never went to Florida that I recall, but we went to, I think, Atlanta once which uh was a little diff…, off the beat and path for us. We usually stayed sort of like East, Northeast, Far West, uh Midwest. So that was a nice uh diversion.
